problems.title: Rank correlations were computed on identifiers
problems.source_location: Table 3 and ranking interpretation, p.9; Tables 4 and 7
claim: Table 3 lists the same \(15\) individual IDs in descending order, but reports Pearson/Spearman \(0.2143\) and Kendall \(0.1429\) as nearly uncorrelated rankings.
analysis: The orderings are \[a=(4,15,5,7,1,8,13,10,11,2,14,6,12,3,9)\] and \[b=(4,15,5,7,8,13,2,11,1,10,12,6,14,9,3)\]. Inverting them to ranks keyed by common ID gives squared displacement sum \(42\). Spearman is \(1-6(42)/(15(15^2-1))=0.925\), also Pearson of rank vectors. The \(11\) discordant and \(94\) concordant pairs give Kendall \(83/105\approx0.790476\), retaining the reported reversal count. Correlating the arbitrary ID arrays directly reproduces \(3/14,3/14,1/7\). Their numerical distances have no ranking meaning.
result: The rankings have substantial agreement. Real reversals remain, and this calculation does not establish which ordering is closer to independently optimal performance.
repair: Invert both orderings to common-ID ranks and report approximately \(0.9250,0.9250,0.7905\). Retain reversals and revise the near-zero-correlation interpretation.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This exact correction reverses a central quantitative argument for severe fitness-ranking distortion.

problems.title: HSIC transport can favor teacher disagreement
claim: The loss minimizes transport cost using HSIC inner-product similarity directly, charging greater association more.
analysis: Use three teacher groups with logit columns \(x_1=(5,2\log0.9,2\log0.1)\), \(x_2=(-1,2,-1)/\sqrt2\), \(x_3=\sqrt{3/2}(-1,0,1)\). Unique argmax coordinates give the required class groups. The latter vectors are centered orthogonal with squared norm \(3\), so their HSIC submatrix is \(I_2\). At temperature \(2\), teacher non-target distribution is \(p=(0.9,0.1)\). Matching it requires diagonal coupling mass at least \(0.8\), hence cost \(0.8\); swapped student \((0.1,0.9)\) admits zero-cost off-diagonal coupling. Swapping those logits preserves target probability and target-category loss, so the distillation component prefers disagreement by \(0.8\beta\), \(\beta>0\).
result: This contradicts the intended guidance component, not the full fusion objective. Appendix datasets using KL instead of HSIC are excluded.
repair: For \(F_i=HK_iH/C\), use \(d_{ij}=\|F_i-F_j\|_F=\sqrt{M_{ii}+M_{jj}-2M_{ij}}\), a metric on distinct representations and a pseudometric when they coincide. Matching then costs zero and swapping \(0.8\sqrt2\). Full retraining remains unvalidated.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: An in-domain teacher construction directly contradicts the central proposed guidance-loss mechanism with target loss unchanged.

problems.title: Teacher alignment can fail by view and sample
problems.source_location: code/train_tree_youtube.py, loss loop around lines 65–78; code/new_loss.py, separated-loss entry
claim: Stored lambdas share a late-bound view index; each batch also gathers a prefix of the full teacher array from batch size alone.
analysis: After constructing views \(0,1\), both lambdas can use final index \(1\). Independently, a batch with sample IDs \((2,3)\) gathers teacher rows \((0,1)\), despite compatible shapes. A single view and full-batch original-order training are passing special cases; the released minibatch path has neither guarantee.
result: The current path need not distill from the same view/sample. Historical checkpoint and table effects remain unknown.
repair: Bind each view/teacher/cost at construction. Carry stable sample IDs or aligned teacher batches through joint shuffling; do not gather a global prefix again.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: These are local release correspondence defects without identified historical experiment damage.

problems.title: YouTubeFace test labels enter selection
problems.source_location: Section 4 evaluation protocol; code/train_tree_youtube.py, lines 34–37 and 91–107; code/gen_offspring_tree.py
claim: Test labels are passed as validation labels; maximum validation accuracy selects checkpoints and evolutionary fitness.
analysis: The dependency reaches the returned architecture even without test gradients. Two independent one-example test scores with success probability \(1/2\) each have expected score \(1/2\), but their selected maximum has expectation \(3/4\). This illustrates selection optimism, not its size here. Outer test folds do not remove within-fold selection dependence. Other datasets explicitly have validation splits and are not automatically implicated.
result: The released selected-test score is not untouched evaluation. An unpublished independent final test could alter the historical conclusion.
repair: Use inner validation for teachers, checkpoints and evolutionary fitness within each outer training split. Freeze selection before outer-test evaluation; corrected scores require re-evaluation.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The demonstrated dependency is bounded to an identified dataset/release; no quantitative inflation or universal benchmark failure is inferred.
